rationale: The Fed held at 3.50-3.75% on a 9-3 vote with three dissents FOR an immediate hike, and Warsh refused to rule out September. BTC popped above $64,400, tagged $64,752, then bled all evening back through the $64,000 shelf it had defended since the overnight reclaim - it now sits at $63,727, below the EMA20/50/100/200 on 15m, 1h, 4h AND daily. Equities closed hard down (QQQ -2.04%, VOO -1.52%), US10Y jumped to 4.688%, Brent to $90.14, and ETF flows logged a fifth straight outflow day. The desk's own reduce rail ($63,000 on a 4H close) has NOT fired and the $62,200 invalidation holds, so selling the long-term core into the range mid would break the framework. Instead the wallet keeps its 0.00336315 BTC core and puts its idle cash to work as a SMALL overnight hedge: $33 notional short at 3x, stop $64,350 (the daily-EMA20 reclaim that would kill the bearish tilt), targets $63,000 and $62,700. That cuts net long exposure roughly 15% through a gap window loaded with MSFT/META after-hours digestion, Q2 GDP + core PCE at 08:30 ET, the BoE decision and AAPL/AMZN tomorrow night. Longs are crowded at a 1.56 long/short account ratio with funding still positive and today's realized liquidations already skew to longs ($7.5M vs $5.5M) with the biggest cluster at $63,500 - exactly the shelf price is resting on.

message.text: You inherit a hedged book, not a flat one: spot core 0.00336315 BTC plus a small $33 3x SHORT with its stop at $64,350 and targets $63,000 / $62,700. Two jobs at 02:00. First, check whether the 4H closed under $63,000 - if it did, the range broke and the hedge should be pressed, not closed. If instead price reclaimed and HELD $64,350, the hedge is wrong: close it and go back to accumulating. Second, remember the overnight calendar is stacked - MSFT/META after-hours, then Q2 GDP and core PCE at 08:30 ET plus the BoE. Cash is nearly all deployed, so do not plan a big tranche; mark the books, resolve the hedge, and keep the $61,900 spot stop live.

lesson.pattern: Crypto holding its ground while equities sell off, measured in the hours BEFORE a binary macro event, is not proof of relative strength.
lesson.insight: Midday leaned bullish precisely on that divergence - BTC defending $64,000 while QQQ ran -0.67% and VOO -0.80% - and it resolved the other way: after the print BTC capitulated to the equity tape instead of leading it, fully retracing the $64,752 spike within four hours. A pre-event divergence measures an unhedged crowd waiting, not conviction. Wait for the event to resolve before letting a divergence set the tilt.
